title: Yamini's verdicts never reach Cratio
body: Qualification verdicts are written to MongoDB and shown on the overview dashboard, but nothing writes them back to Cratio CRM. The four AI Bot fields on the lead record have been null since Aug 2025, so sales never sees the qualification and the pipeline is read-only in practice. The workflow that would close this loop, KW 3 · Qualification & CRM Writeback (ppXd4bTAUtLaBwB7), exists in n8n and is inactive.

title: LeadQ's Atlas credentials belong to a departed employee, username reused as password
body: The MongoDB Atlas connection string is hardcoded in the LeadQ config and the account belongs to someone who has left. The username is reused as the password. Rotate in Atlas first, then update the config and restart the unit, then audit Atlas access logs. This cannot be verified from a VPS dump because the cluster is external.

title: LeadQ and Overview read different databases and nobody knows which is true
body: Yamini writes to the local MongoDB. LeadQ reads MongoDB Atlas whatsapp_leads2. Nothing observed connects the two. Either Atlas has been frozen since the April migration and the sales floor has served stale data for four months, or a second pipeline is still writing to it and two dashboards are reporting different numbers for the same agent. Compare the newest document timestamp in each database to settle it.

title: MongoDB was listening on 0.0.0.0 with 26k customer conversations behind it
body: Reported on 18 Aug against srv1340120: mongod bound to all interfaces with no firewall in front of it. Recorded here so the fix is traceable rather than silently dropped.

body: Reported on 18 Aug against the second n8n host.

title: Media server offers a public directory listing on 0.0.0.0:8899
body: media-server.service runs `python3 -m http.server 8899 --directory /var/www/media` bound to all interfaces. Python's http.server serves an index of the directory when no index file is present. Bind it to 127.0.0.1 and proxy through nginx if it needs to be public.

title: overview.leadq.co.in terminates TLS but certbot holds no certificate for it
body: nginx declares listen 443 ssl for this hostname, but the certbot inventory has no certificate covering it. The leadq.co.in certificate covers the apex, www and hrportal only. Whatever it is presenting on 443 is worth checking before a browser starts warning about it.

title: Eight overlapping WhatsApp workflows, two sharing an identical name
body: Two workflows are both named KW WhatsApp — Main with different ids, alongside six more inbound responders of overlapping purpose. Nobody can tell from the n8n list which one is authoritative. Consolidate, and rename anything that survives.

title: n8n's SQLite database is 2.5 GB, with a 4.4 GB stale copy beside it
body: The live database.sqlite is 2.5 GB, driven largely by ~100 imported demo workflows and unpruned execution data. A 4.4 GB n8n-db-2026-08-17.sqlite also sits in /root, and a 905 MB backup archive beside it. Set EXECUTIONS_DATA_MAX_AGE, prune, and delete the stale copies.

title: Agent conversations and dashboard sign-in share one database
body: allowedUsers and authLogs live in the same Yamini database as customerChats. Read access to the sign-in allowlist is read access to every customer conversation. Split the auth collections out.

title: Meta CAPI is inactive while Google Enhanced Conversions is live, the reverse of the architecture brief
body: The architecture brief describes Meta CAPI as the live attribution path and Google Enhanced Conversions as planned. The n8n state is the opposite. Recorded as a contradiction rather than resolved silently: one of the two sources is wrong and it needs a human decision which.

title: A scheduled job on srv1340120 carries a credential on its command line
body: The claude-deploy crontab entry "0 3 * * *" passes a secret as an argument, which makes it visible in the process table and in shell history. Move it to an environment file with 0600 permissions.

title: A scheduled job on srv1340120 carries a credential on its command line
body: The root crontab entry "0 2 * * 0" passes a secret as an argument, which makes it visible in the process table and in shell history. Move it to an environment file with 0600 permissions.
